description: PROVISIONAL default rules for observed AI-agent actions (docs/skill/spec-draft.md, S2). Every rule here is a starting point for the owner to confirm or change; none is an approved company policy. Built-in invariants (kill switch, disputed attribution, critical findings, agent configuration changes, security tool tampering) deny before these rules and cannot be relaxed here. An unparseable command is never allowed: where these rules would allow it the engine asks instead, and a deny these rules give it stays a deny. Assistant-specific instruction-file and settings paths are not named in this vendor-neutral file: add them to agent_config_paths in the deployment's ruleset.

rules.description: Reads, prompts, session start/end and turn ends are allowed when the session is tied to a person who resolves now in the identity store and the attribution is verified (a declared person, whose claim nobody vouched for, is asked). Credential reads are still denied by the credential rule below, which is stricter.
A shell command made only of known readers with only safe options (read_only_command) is a read: allowed for a known, verified person's organizational or employee-operated agent (declared is asked).
Any push that lands on a protected branch (main, master, release/*, prod*), or whose branch cannot be told, needs the person's confirmation.
A force push (including deleting or mirroring refs) to any branch needs the person's confirmation, so the scanned-push allow below never covers one. Protected branches are denied by the next rule.
Force pushes (including deleting or mirroring refs) to a protected branch are denied. An unknown branch counts as protected.
Rewriting history (rebase, amend, hard reset, filter-branch, forced branch moves) on a protected branch is denied. An unknown branch counts as protected.
Reading or copying credentials (keys, tokens, .env files, credential stores, environment dumps) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Running code fetched from the network (download piped to a shell, fetched then executed) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Raising privilege (sudo, runas, setuid, adding administrators, privileged containers) is denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.

Commands that hide what they run (decoded payloads piped to a shell, encoded commands, disguised program names) or that set variables choosing what code runs are denied for employee-operated agents and agents of unknown class.
Sending or fetching data over the network from a shell needs the person's confirmation.
Installing packages or running package runners needs the person's confirmation.
When no person can be tied to the session (attribution unknown), every write, shell command, push, connector call, fetch, sub-agent and other tool use is denied.
Agents the registry marks suspended or retired may not do anything that is not a read.
File writes, edits, commits and pushes are inspected first; a secret finding of high severity or worse denies the action. A missing or incomplete inspection denies it too (missing_inspection).
A shell command that commits or pushes is inspected first; a secret finding of high severity or worse denies it, and so does a missing or incomplete inspection.

A recursive copy or move, a sync or an archive extraction into the current directory, a parent, the home directory, a root or an unknown place needs the person's confirmation: it can plant files, agent configuration among them, that no path rule sees.

A push or commit whose scan found anything of high severity or worse (a secret, failed tests, a failed sandbox check, a sensitive path) is denied. A missing or incomplete scan denies it too (missing_inspection).

A plain push (the git_push kind, which the intake gives only to one plain git push naming at most one branch) whose scan is complete is allowed for a known, verified person's organizational or employee-operated agent (a declared person, whose claim nobody vouched for, is asked). High findings deny it (rule above), protected or unknown branches and force pushes ask, and a shell command that pushes is never allowed by this rule.
Recursive or irreversible deletion needs the person's confirmation.
